title: Cisco Duo Admin Login Unusual Browser
exclusions: Covers Duo Admin Panel sign-ins only, not end-user authentications to protected applications.
evidence: Alert rows with administrator, source IP, location, browser, OS, and outcome, kept with the analyst's verdict.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Sign in to the Duo Admin Panel as a test administrator from a browser outside the expected list. After the next input interval the activity event appears with `action.name=admin_login`, and the search returns one row for that administrator.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Sign in again from an expected browser. The activity event is indexed, but the search returns no row for it.

dataSources: `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:activity` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input, Activity log type, which polls `GET /admin/v2/logs/activity`. One event per user or administrator action, with the access device's browser, OS, IP address, and location.
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Cisco Duo input. Replaces the deprecated Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026).
spl:
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:activity" "action.name"=admin_login NOT access_device.browser IN (Chrome)
| rename actor.name as user access_device.ip.address as src_ip
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by access_device.browser access_device.browser_version src_ip access_device.location.city access_device.location.country access_device.location.state access_device.os access_device.os_version actor.details actor.type outcome.result user
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
description: Finds Duo Admin Panel sign-ins (`action.name=admin_login`) whose browser is outside the expected set for your administrators. Each row shows the administrator, source IP, location, browser, OS, and outcome.
value: Administrators run a small, predictable set of browsers. A Duo Admin Panel login from an unexpected browser often means a stolen session or credentials used from attacker tooling, and Duo administrators can switch off MFA for everyone.
implementation: Collect the Duo Activity log with the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input into `index=duo`. Replace the expected value in the `NOT ... IN (...)` clause with the browsers your administrators are approved to use. Alert on each row; investigate successful logins first.
visualization: Alert table: firstTime, user, src_ip, access_device.location.country, access_device.browser, access_device.os, outcome.result. Supporting map: admin sign-ins by country over 30 days.

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Unlisted but legitimate browser values** — the shipped search expects one value. Administrators who travel or use a second platform will match until you list every approved value.

2. **VPN and cloud egress** — admins behind a corporate VPN or secure web gateway appear with the egress location, which can sit in another country or show a generic browser string.

3. **Failed attempts** — rows with `outcome.result` other than success are still worth review but are lower priority than successful sign-ins.

**Suppression:** a lookup of administrators and their approved values, joined before the `NOT` filter.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs. It replaces the Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026); disable the old connector's inputs after cutover so events are not indexed twice.
• A Duo Admin API application created by an Owner-role administrator in the Duo Admin Panel under Applications > Protect an Application > Admin API. Record the integration key, secret key, and API hostname (`api-XXXXXXXX.duosecurity.com`), and grant it **Grant read log**.
• Outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) from the input host to the API hostname, and an accurate system clock on that host, because the Admin API signs every request with the current date.
• An index for Duo data (this page uses `index=duo`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the identity and SOC teams.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Cisco Duo card, and create an input with the integration key, secret key, and API hostname. Enable the Activity log type and set the index to `duo`.
• The input reads `GET /admin/v2/logs/activity` and writes `sourcetype=cisco:duo:activity`: nested JSON with `action.name`, `actor.name`, `actor.type`, `target.name`, `target.details`, `old_target.details`, `outcome.result`, and `access_device.*` (browser, OS, IP address, city, state, country).
• Check the field this search needs: run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:activity "action.name"=admin_login | stats count by access_device.browser` over 30 days to see the values your administrators actually use.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:activity" "action.name"=admin_login NOT access_device.browser IN (Chrome)
| rename actor.name as user access_device.ip.address as src_ip
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by access_device.browser access_device.browser_version src_ip access_device.location.city access_device.location.country access_device.location.state access_device.os access_device.os_version actor.details actor.type outcome.result user
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
```

Understanding this SPL
• `"action.name"=admin_login` keeps only Duo Admin Panel sign-ins; the quotes are needed because the field name contains a dot.
• `NOT access_device.browser IN (Chrome)` removes the expected browser; edit the list from the 30-day check in Step 1.
• `actor.name` (the administrator) and `access_device.ip.address` are renamed to `user` and `src_ip` so the row lines up with other identity alerts.
• Every `by` field must exist on the event, otherwise `stats` drops it. If your events lack `actor.details` or state, remove those fields from the `by` clause.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Duo admin console (Admin Panel) under Reports > Administrator Actions, filtered to admin logins, for the same time range.
• Pick one known administrator sign-in and check that country, browser, and OS on the event match what the administrator used.
• Run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:activity | timechart span=1h count` over 7 days to confirm there are no collection gaps.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Schedule every 15 minutes over the last 20 minutes; throttle on `user` plus `src_ip` for 12 hours.
• The responder confirms the sign-in with the administrator out of band. If it is not recognized, reset the admin's password and hardware token and review Reports > Administrator Actions for changes made in that session.
• Send to Enterprise Security as a finding on `user` when ES is in use.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No Duo events and HTTP 401 in the input log under `$SPLUNK_HOME/var/log/splunk/duo_splunkapp/`: wrong secret key, an API hostname from a different Duo account, or clock skew on the input host.
• HTTP 403: the Admin API application is missing **Grant read log**.
• HTTP 429: Duo rate-limits the log endpoints. Make sure the deprecated 3504 connector and the 7404 input are not both polling the same Admin API application.
• Duplicate rows after migration: the 3504 connector and the 7404 input are both enabled for the same log type.
• Events arrive but `access_device.*` fields are empty: the activity record has no device context for that action. Admin logins normally carry it; check one raw event.
grandmaExplanation: We watch how people sign in to the Duo control panel and flag logins from a web browser our admins never use.
